comments.author: home
comments.text:
GOAL: make Markus Markdown the CANONICAL article body, and project it into what Pretext needs.

THE CORE ARCHITECTURAL FACT (verified in lib/articles.ts):
  Article.body: string[]        <- flat plain-text paragraphs, no inline markup
  Article.pullQuotes?: string[] <- SIDE-CHANNEL array, not positioned in the body
  Article.assets/image/video    <- also side-channel, positioned by the solver

Markus's directive vocabulary (pull-quote, card-grid, card, two-up, column, figure, callout, details, aside, metric, timeline) is a strict SUPERSET of that, and it is POSITIONAL - the pull quote sits where the author put it. So the resolution is not to invent a Papyrus schema; it is to adopt Markus's vocabulary as the Papyrus content schema.

DIRECTION OF TRAVEL:
  Article.body: string[]  ->  Article.body: string (Markus Markdown)
  Article.pullQuotes[]    ->  DELETED; pull quotes become :::pull-quote in the body

SCOPE:
1. Consume the Markus document IR (kanbus-37dd9a, in the Markus repo, gives typed block nodes + schema_version). Do NOT re-parse Markdown in TypeScript.
2. Build the Pretext PROJECTION: IR -> the flat structures the solver consumes (ordered paragraph strings, extracted pull quotes, figures). This projection is LOSSY BY DESIGN and that is correct - Pretext cannot express a card-grid. Decide and document the degradation for each directive Pretext cannot render (best candidate: render its textual content inline, never silently drop content).
3. Type the IR in TS from the schema Markus emits. Keep schema_version checked at the boundary; fail loudly on mismatch.
4. Round-trip test: an existing article migrated to Markdown must project back to the SAME body: string[] it has today. That is the regression proof for PPY-b794e1.

DEPENDS ON: kanbus-37dd9a (Markus document IR) and PPY-d79ff2 (Renderer interface).

comments.author: home
comments.text:
UNBLOCKED ON THE MARKUS SIDE: kanbus-37dd9a is landed and reviewed (Markus repo, branch feature/document-ir). 'markus ast' now emits a typed, versioned IR - schema_version: 1, front matter parsed, and block nodes (heading/paragraph/list/blockquote/code/table/thematic_break/html) sitting as ordered PEERS of directive nodes in one children[]. Inline content is typed too (text/emphasis/strong/strikethrough/code_span/link/image/breaks).

NOTE: inline code spans are type 'code_span', distinct from block-level 'code'. Do not conflate them in the TS types.

I PROTOTYPED THE PROJECTION AGAINST THE REAL IR - it works. Verified output for an article with front matter + pull-quote + card-grid:

  body (string[]):
    'Developers are learning that reliable agents need less freedom, not more.'
    'Across demos and tool launches, builders kept circling the same answer.'
    'Planning state'
    'Read-only tools.'
    'Implementation state'
    'Edit tools.'
    'The lesson is not that agents are over.'
  pullQuotes: ['The practical breakthrough is not giving agents a bigger sandbox.']
  degraded directives (content preserved inline): ['card-grid','card','card']

The algorithm: walk children in order; paragraph -> push inline_text() to body; heading -> push its text to body; directive pull-quote -> push to pullQuotes; ANY OTHER directive -> recurse into its children so content is preserved inline and NOTHING is silently dropped. That last rule is the important one and it is the documented degradation policy.

Port this to TypeScript against the typed IR. The Python prototype is a proof of shape, not the deliverable.

STILL BLOCKED BY: PPY-d79ff2 (Renderer interface) - the projection needs somewhere to live.

comments.text:
## PPY-a10206 implementation plan (Composer 2.5 — PLAN ONLY)

**Status:** Ready to implement in an isolated worktree. Blocker PPY-d79ff2 is closed (`f9b073f` on `feature/renderer-architecture`). Markus document IR (`kanbus-37dd9a`, `schema_version: 1`) is landed on Markus `feature/document-ir`.

---

### Nomenclature (do not relitigate)

Per PPY-93a9c0 / PPY-92f846:

- **Renderer** = swappable pipeline (`pretext` | `markus`)
- **Layout** = Pretext-internal look (`newsprint` | `blog` | `magazine`)
- **Publication** = title/property (P.apyr.us, Threat Intelligence, Pilobol.us)

This task delivers the **Pretext projection layer** (IR → flat solver inputs). It does **not** implement a Renderer, change `lib/renderer.ts`, or touch `renderers/pretext/`.

---

### Worktree (create only when authorized)

| | |
|---|---|
| **Path** | `/Users/home/Projects/Papyrus-worktrees/PPY-a10206-projection` |
| **Branch** | `cursor/feature/PPY-a10206-pretext-projection-3af6` |
| **Base** | `origin/feature/renderer-architecture` (after `git fetch origin feature/renderer-architecture`) |

**Never implement in the primary clone** (`/Users/home/Projects/Papyrus`) — it has dirty leftovers from a dead agent.

```bash
cd /Users/home/Projects/Papyrus
git fetch origin feature/renderer-architecture
git worktree add -b cursor/feature/PPY-a10206-pretext-projection-3af6 \
  /Users/home/Projects/Papyrus-worktrees/PPY-a10206-projection \
  origin/feature/renderer-architecture
```

---

### Step 0 — Recover leftovers (rsync, then review; do not trust blindly)

From primary clone → worktree:

```bash
rsync -av \
  /Users/home/Projects/Papyrus/lib/markus-ir.ts \
  /Users/home/Projects/Papyrus/lib/markus-projection.ts \
  /Users/home/Projects/Papyrus/scripts/test-markus-projection.ts \
  /Users/home/Projects/Papyrus-worktrees/PPY-a10206-projection/lib/ \
  # (adjust paths: fixtures go to scripts/fixtures/)
rsync -av /Users/home/Projects/Papyrus/scripts/fixtures/ \
  /Users/home/Projects/Papyrus-worktrees/PPY-a10206-projection/scripts/fixtures/
# package.json: cherry-pick only the test:markus-projection script line
```

**Review checklist against issue requirements:**

| Requirement | Leftover status | Action |
|---|---|---|
| Typed IR from real `markus ast` output, not hand-invented | `lib/markus-ir.ts` + `scripts/fixtures/markus-sample.ast.json` | Re-capture fixture with live `markus ast` on Markus `feature/document-ir`; diff against committed JSON |
| `schema_version: 1` fail-loud boundary | `parseMarkusDocument` + `MarkusSchemaVersionError` | Keep; test already asserts mismatch throws |
| `code_span` (inline) ≠ `code` (block) | Separate types + test assertion on sample | Keep; verify against `markusmd/blocks.py` `CodeSpan` vs `CodeBlock` |
| Degradation: directives Pretext can't express → recurse children; nothing silently dropped | `directiveDegradedText` + `leafDirectiveText` fallback | Keep; add explicit test that degraded directive names are surfaced if we want observability (optional `degradedDirectives: string[]` — only if useful for PPY-b794e1 migration script, not required for solver) |
| `pull-quote` → `pullQuotes[]` (not body) | Implemented | Keep |
| `figure` → `images[]` as `ArticleImageAsset` | Implemented | Keep |
| Round-trip: migrated article projects to same `body: string[]` | **GAP** — sample fixture only, no seed-article round-trip | **Must add** (see Step 2) |

Leftover smoke test already passes on primary clone: `npm run test:markus-projection` ✅

---

### Step 1 — Deliverables (in scope)

**New modules (lib/, no renderer wiring yet):**

1. **`lib/markus-ir.ts`** — TS mirror of Markus `Document.to_dict()` shape:
   - `MARKUS_IR_SCHEMA_VERSION = 1`
   - Inline union: `text | emphasis | strong | strikethrough | code_span | link | image | soft_break | hard_break | html_inline`
   - Block union: `heading | paragraph | list | blockquote | code | thematic_break | html | table`
   - Directive nodes as ordered peers in `children[]`
   - `parseMarkusDocument(raw)` — only untyped ingress point; throws `MarkusSchemaVersionError` on mismatch

2. **`lib/markus-projection.ts`** — `projectMarkusDocumentToPretext()`:
   - Output: `{ body: string[]; pullQuotes: string[]; images: ArticleImageAsset[] }`
   - Walk `document.children` in order
   - **Lossy by design** — document the policy in module header (already drafted)
   - **Non-negotiable degradation rule:** any directive Pretext cannot render (`card-grid`, `two-up`, `callout`, …) recurses into children; leaf directives (`metric`, `video`) degrade to stringified attributes; never silently drop

**Tests & fixtures:**

3. **`scripts/fixtures/markus-sample.md`** + **`markus-sample.ast.json`** — directive mix fixture (pull-quote, card-grid, two-up, figure, inline `code_span` vs block `code`). Regenerate `.ast.json` via `markus ast` (not hand-edited).

4. **`scripts/test-markus-projection.ts`** + **`package.json`** script `test:markus-projection`

---

### Step 2 — Close the round-trip gap (required for acceptance)

Issue acceptance: *"an existing article migrated to Markdown must project back to the SAME `body: string[]` it has today"* (regression proof for PPY-b794e1).

The synthetic `markus-sample` proves directive degradation shape but is **not** a seed-article round-trip.

**Add:**

- `scripts/fixtures/agent-procedure-patterns.md` — Markus Markdown migration of `lib/articles.ts` → `articles[0]` (`slug: "agent-procedure-patterns"`). Pull quotes become positional `:::pull-quote` directives; body paragraphs map 1:1. Must pass `markus validate`.
- `scripts/fixtures/agent-procedure-patterns.ast.json` — `markus ast` capture
- Extend `scripts/test-markus-projection.ts`:
  - `projectMarkusJsonToPretext(ast)` → `body` deep-equals `articles[0].body`
  - `pullQuotes` deep-equals `articles[0].pullQuotes`
  - Assert pull-quote text does **not** also appear in `body` (side-channel invariant)

If editorial positioning makes exact `body[]` match impossible for the full article, start with a **minimal excerpt fixture** cut from that article (N paragraphs + 1 pull-quote) where migration is unambiguous — but prefer the full `agent-procedure-patterns` article since it is all plain paragraphs (no lists/tables to flatten differently).

---

### Step 3 — Verification (re-run locally; do not trust subagent reports)

In the worktree only:

```bash
npm run typecheck
npm run lint
npm run test:markus-projection
```

**Cross-repo preflight:** Markus `feature/document-ir` pip-installed editable; `markus ast --version` / `markus ast scripts/fixtures/markus-sample.md` must succeed before trusting fixtures.

**Do not chase:** `npm run build` Collecting-page-data failure (pre-existing, no AppSync backend — PPY-6b4094).

---

### Step 4 — Commit & PR (when authorized)

- Branch: `cursor/feature/PPY-a10206-pretext-projection-3af6`
- One focused commit (or two: lib + tests/fixtures)
- PR into `develop` (or stack on `feature/renderer-architecture` per Ryan's push policy — **do not push without explicit authorization**)
- `git diff --stat` sanity: only `lib/markus-*.ts`, `scripts/`, `package.json` — nothing in `renderers/`, `amplify/`, `project/`

---

### Explicitly out of scope (this issue)

| Item | Owner |
|---|---|
| `lib/renderer.ts` contract changes | — |
| `renderers/pretext/` rewrite | — |
| Markus renderer / static HTML build | PPY-88f77b |
| `Article.body: string[]` → `string` schema change | PPY-b794e1 |
| Content migration script | PPY-b794e1 |
| Wiring projection into `graphql-content-repository` / solver call sites | Follow-on after b794e1 |
| Hosting / Amplify sandbox | PPY-17fcfc / PPY-6b4094 |

---

### Risks & notes

1. **Cross-repo hazard:** Papyrus depends on unpushed Markus `feature/document-ir`. Fixture regeneration fails on another machine without it.
2. **Primary clone hygiene:** After rsync, leave primary-clone files untracked/uncommitted — do not `git add -A` on primary.
3. **List/table flattening:** `blockText` for lists emits one body line per list item; seed articles are paragraph-only today, so round-trip on `agent-procedure-patterns` is safe. Document that list/table round-trip semantics may differ — migration script (b794e1) must account for this.
4. **`figure` vs `article.image`:** Projection extracts `figure` directives to `images[]`; legacy `Article.image` is unchanged in this task. Full asset unification is b794e1+.
5. **No `project/` commits** in implementation PR.

---

### Implementation order

1. Create worktree from `origin/feature/renderer-architecture`
2. Rsync + review leftovers
3. Re-capture `markus-sample.ast.json` from live `markus ast`
4. Add seed-article round-trip fixture + test (close acceptance gap)
5. typecheck → lint → test:markus-projection
6. Commit, push (when authorized), PR, comment verification results on this issue
